items.title: The Unlived Life
items.question: Socrates declared one kind of life not worth living for a human being. Which life?
items.correctExplanation: Unexamined life — living unquestioned forfeits humanity's signature act: reflection. Examination dignifies existence.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is unexamined life. Apology's sentence stands: unscrutinized living wastes humanness. Worth requires wondering first.
items.lessonContent:
Worth requires wondering first always.
Unscrutinized living wastes humanness.
Reflection dignifies bare existence.
Examination is humanity's signature.
Share this: examine one hour today.

items.title: The Wise Ignorance
items.question: Oracle-named wisest, Socrates found only one thing he knew. What was his sole expertise?
items.correctExplanation: His ignorance — knowing the extent of not-knowing: wisdom as measured lack. Experts overflow; Socrates empties.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is his ignorance. Craftsmen knew trades but pretended to wisdom; Socrates knew neither, and knew it. Measured lack beats unmeasured surplus.
items.lessonContent:
Measured lack beats unmeasured surplus.
Knowing limits constitutes wisdom here.
Experts overflow; sages empty usefully.
Ignorance owned outperforms knowledge feigned.
Share this: own one ignorance proudly.

items.title: The Refuting Walk
items.question: Socrates asked definitions, drew out contradictions, and left interlocutors improvedly puzzled. What is this method?
items.correctExplanation: Elenchus — refutation by questioning: premises granted, contradictions derived, conceit purged. Midwifery through embarrassment.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is elenchus. Lectures inform; elenchus transforms by refuting: interlocutors birth truth through aporia. Puzzlement is progress here.
items.lessonContent:
Puzzlement marks progress truly here.
Refutation purges conceit reliably.
Questions birth truths lectures abort.
Midwifery embarrasses productively.
Share this: refute one conceit kindly.

items.title: The Stinging Insect
items.question: Athens dozed like a sluggish horse; Socrates claimed heaven sent something to sting it awake. What was he?
items.correctExplanation: Gadfly — heaven-sent irritant to drowsy democracy: stinging steeds into motion. Annoyance as civic duty.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is gadfly. Horses doze; flies bite awake: Socrates appointed himself Athens' alarm. Civic duty stings sometimes.
items.lessonContent:
Alarms annoy sleepers necessarily.
Stings wake drowsy democracies.
Heaven sends irritants purposefully.
Civic duty buzzes persistently.
Share this: sting one slumber kindly.

items.title: The Tended Soul
items.question: Wealth and reputation mean nothing, Socrates urged, beside caring for one thing above all. What deserves supreme care?
items.correctExplanation: Their souls — care of psyche over property: Apology's economics inverts Athens' ledger. Souls appreciate; fortunes rust.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is their souls. Wealth rusts, reputations fade, souls compound: Socratic portfolio theory. Tend interiors before exteriors.
items.lessonContent:
Interiors compound; exteriors rust fully.
Souls appreciate with tending daily.
Portfolios invert Athenian ledgers.
Care within outlasts wealth without.
Share this: tend one soul today.

items.title: The Knowing Virtue
items.question: Socrates scandalously identified virtue with a cognitive state — vice being mere ignorance. What is virtue?
items.correctExplanation: Knowledge — virtue as understanding the good: knowers act well necessarily. Ethics reduces to epistemology boldly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is knowledge. Habits, commandments, and sentiments miss it: Socratic intellectualism makes wrongdoing a cognitive bug. Teach goodness; behavior follows.
items.lessonContent:
Wrongdoing debugs as ignorance here.
Understanding necessitates right action.
Epistemology grounds ethics boldly.
Teach goodness; watch behavior follow.
Share this: know one good fully.

items.title: The Willing Wrong
items.question: If virtue is knowledge, wrongdoing must be involuntary — error, never malice. Who does evil on purpose?
items.correctExplanation: Nobody willingly — all wrongdoers mistake goods: apparent benefit deceives choosers. Malice dissolves into miscalculation.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is nobody willingly. Volunteers for evil vanish under analysis: everyone aims at seeming good. Mistakes explain monsters fully.
items.lessonContent:
Seeming goods deceive all choosers.
Monsters mistake; none malice purely.
Errors explain evils completely.
Willing wrongs exist nowhere here.
Share this: pity one wrongdoer today.

items.title: The Weak Will
items.question: If virtue is knowledge, why do people act against their better judgment? What threatens intellectualism?
items.correctExplanation: Akrasia — weakness of will: knowing better, doing worse. Appetites veto insights daily.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is akrasia. Judgments lose to appetites nightly: better known gets overruled often. Knowing battles wanting eternally.
items.lessonContent:
Judgments lose to appetites nightly.
Better known gets overruled often.
Weakness challenges intellectualism directly.
Knowing battles wanting eternally.
Share this: strengthen one weak will.

items.title: The Pious Puzzle
items.question: Is conduct pious because gods love it, or loved because pious? What makes piety pious?
items.correctExplanation: Its own nature — gods track goodness; goodness leads. Love follows worth, never founds it.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is its own nature. Dependence directions decide: loved-because-pious grounds divinity in goodness. Natures precede divine approval.
items.lessonContent:
Gods track goodness; goodness leads.
Love follows worth, never founds it.
Natures precede divine approval.
Piety stands independent ever.
Share this: love one good for itself.

items.title: The Search Paradox
items.question: Meno asks: how search for unknown things, unrecognizable even if found? What blocks inquiry?
items.correctExplanation: Inquiry paradox — searching puzzles philosophers: unknowns resist seeking logically. Recognition needs prior acquaintance.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is inquiry paradox. Unknowns resist seeking: neither knowledge nor ignorance can start. Paradoxes stall inquiries initially.
items.lessonContent:
Searching puzzles philosophers deeply.
Unknowns resist seeking logically.
Recognition needs prior acquaintance.
Paradoxes stall inquiries initially.
Share this: seek one unknown bravely.

items.title: The Remembered Truth
items.question: Learning, says Meno's Socrates, is really something else entirely — souls retrieving eternal knowledge. What is learning?
items.correctExplanation: Recollection — souls retrieve eternal truths: learning remembers, never acquires. Eternity tutors temporal minds.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is recollection. Acquisition models fail: latent knowledge awaits prompting. Remembering replaces stocking up.
items.lessonContent:
Souls retrieve eternal truths slowly.
Learning remembers, never acquires.
Latent knowledge awaits prompting.
Eternity tutors temporal minds.
Share this: recall one eternal truth.

items.title: The Geometry Slave
items.question: An uneducated slave boy solves geometry under questioning alone. Who demonstrates innate knowledge?
items.correctExplanation: Slave boy — untutored minds solve geometry: questioning draws latent proofs. Schooling unnecessary for insight.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is slave boy. Schooling absent, insight present: dialogue extracts what teaching never installed. Geometry sleeps in all minds.
items.lessonContent:
Untutored minds solve geometry nightly.
Questioning draws latent proofs.
Schooling unnecessary for insight here.
Geometry sleeps in all minds.
Share this: question one untutored mind.

items.title: The Definition Killer
items.question: Every proposed definition of courage meets cases that break it. What defeats definitions?
items.correctExplanation: Counterexamples surface — cases break neat definitions: courage resists formula. Instances defeat abstractions.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is counterexamples surface. Definitions fall to instances: one brave coward or cowardly hero undoes formulas. Neatness yields to cases.
items.lessonContent:
Cases break neat definitions daily.
Definitions die by example reliably.
Exceptions emerge from inquiry.
Neatness yields to instances.
Share this: counter one definition kindly.

items.title: The Oracle's Riddle
items.question: Declared wisest for knowing his own ignorance, Socrates outranked experts. What constituted his wisdom?
items.correctExplanation: Knows his ignorance — awareness crowns the ignorant: confessed gaps outrank feigned fullness. Oracles praise measured lacks.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is knows his ignorance. Experts overflowed with unexamined certainties; Socrates inventoried emptiness accurately. Wisdom knows its own borders.
items.lessonContent:
Awareness crowns the ignorant truly.
Confessed gaps outrank feigned fullness.
Oracles praise measured lacks.
Wisdom knows its own borders.
Share this: confess one border today.

items.title: The Strange Gods
items.question: Athens charged Socrates with introducing new divinities and corrupting youth. What religious crime was alleged?
items.correctExplanation: New divinities — unlicensed gods threatened civic cults: novelty frightened priesthoods. Charges veil politics.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is new divinities. Asebeia alleged foreign worship: strange gods menaced established rites. Accusations veil political motives.
items.lessonContent:
Charges alleged novel worship falsely.
Strange gods threatened civic cults.
Accusations veil political motives.
Novelty frightens established priesthoods.
Share this: tolerate one strange god.

items.title: The Welcome End
items.question: Death is either dreamless sleep or soul migration — Socrates fears neither outcome. Which should frighten him?
items.correctExplanation: Neither option — sleep rests, migration converses: both outcomes welcome. Fear fits neither alternative.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is neither option. Oblivion rests the weary; migration introduces heroes. Apology disarms death both ways.
items.lessonContent:
Sleep rests the weary fully.
Migration converses with heroes.
Fear fits neither outcome ever.
Welcome both alternatives calmly.
Share this: fear neither outcome.

items.title: The Willing Cup
items.question: Socrates drank hemlock conversing cheerfully about immortality. How did he meet death?
items.correctExplanation: Cheerfully drinking — cups emptied conversing: philosophy continued past poison. Willing drinkers teach dying.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is cheerfully drinking. Gloom never entered the cell: dialogue outlasted hemlock. Conversations defeat cups.
items.lessonContent:
Cups emptied conversing calmly.
Cheer accompanies final draughts.
Conversations outlast poison here.
Willing drinkers teach dying.
Share this: drink one cup calmly.

items.title: The Bound Citizen
items.question: Escape arranged, Socrates stayed to drink the cup. What bound him to Athens' verdict?
items.correctExplanation: Laws' authority — verdicts bind consenting citizens: residence implies agreement. Authority legitimized by dwelling.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is laws' authority. Agreements outlive advantages: citizens owe obedience reciprocally. Escape would wrong the laws that raised him.
items.lessonContent:
Verdicts bind consenting citizens fully.
Agreements outlive advantages personally.
Citizens owe obedience reciprocally.
Authority legitimized by residence.
Share this: honor one hard verdict.

items.title: The Better Wound
items.question: Socrates claimed suffering injustice surpasses doing it. Which fate is preferable?
items.correctExplanation: Suffering it — endured wrongs outrank inflicted ones: victims keep cleaner souls. Doing stains; suffering ennobles.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is suffering it. Inflicting corrupts agents; enduring preserves them. Preferable fates favor patients over perpetrators.
items.lessonContent:
Endured wrongs outrank inflicted ones.
Victims keep cleaner souls here.
Doing stains; suffering ennobles.
Preferable fates favor patients.
Share this: suffer one wrong nobly.

items.title: The Stronger Fallacy
items.question: Thrasymachus defined justice as the advantage of the stronger. What does this reduce morality to?
items.correctExplanation: Power worship — strength defines right absurdly: rulers flattered, justice voided. Might makes wrong.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is power worship. Advantage-of-stronger enthrones bullying: morality collapses into flattery. Strong wrongs never make rights.
items.lessonContent:
Strength defines right absurdly here.
Rulers flattered corrupt justice fully.
Might makes wrong, never right.
Advantage worship degrades morals.
Share this: defy one strong wrong.

items.title: The Loving Ladder
items.question: Diotima's ladder climbs from beautiful bodies to Beauty itself. What ascends?
items.correctExplanation: Eros ascending — ladders climb toward Beauty: bodies begin, absolutes complete. Desire educates upward.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is eros ascending. Bodies start what Beauty finishes: love climbs rungs of loveliness. Ascents transform appetites.
items.lessonContent:
Ladders climb toward Beauty steadily.
Bodies begin; Beauty completes.
Desire ascends rungs of loveliness.
Climbing loves reach absolutes.
Share this: climb one rung lovingly.

items.title: The Known Self
items.question: Alcibiades learned that caring for oneself requires first knowing something. What must be known?
items.correctExplanation: Oneself — knowing precedes caring: selves studied yield tended souls. First know, then tend.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is oneself. Care without knowledge misfires: comprehension precedes cultivation. Selves known get tended well.
items.lessonContent:
Knowing precedes caring always.
Selves studied yield tended souls.
Care follows comprehension reliably.
First know, then tend fully.
Share this: know one self better.

items.title: The Dying Art
items.question: Philosophy, says Phaedo's Socrates, is practice for a final separation. What does it rehearse?
items.correctExplanation: Dying practice — rehearsals prepare final separations: souls practice leaving bodies. Philosophy trains farewells.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is dying practice. Separations rehearsed lose terror: practiced farewells free minds. Training outlasts trembling.
items.lessonContent:
Rehearsals prepare final separations.
Souls practice leaving bodies.
Philosophy trains farewells daily.
Separation rehearsed loses terror.
Share this: rehearse one farewell.

items.title: The Unharmed Soul
items.question: A better man cannot be harmed by a worse, Socrates claimed at trial. What can't touch him?
items.correctExplanation: Real harm — better souls resist damage: worse men harm themselves only. Virtue armors inwardly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is real harm. Verdicts wound bodies, never souls: goodness insulates essence. Harmlessness crowns the just.
items.lessonContent:
Better souls resist damage fully.
Worse men harm themselves only.
Virtue armors against true injury.
Harmlessness crowns goodness here.
Share this: harm no better soul.

items.title: The Ruling Wisdom
items.question: Plato's Republic crowns lovers of wisdom as rulers of the just city. Who should govern?
items.correctExplanation: Philosopher-kings — wisdom should rule cities: lovers of truth govern best. Knowledge crowns governance.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is philosopher-kings. Warriors fight, producers make, thinkers rule: each part performs its nature. Cities mirror souls hierarchically.
items.lessonContent:
Wisdom should rule cities justly.
Lovers of truth govern best.
Rulers thinking beat warriors fighting.
Knowledge crowns governance ideally.
Share this: elect wisdom once.
